red_flags.title: Fictitious / Phantom Revenue Invoicing Without Cleared Bank Cash (AUTO-INV-2026-0006)
red_flags.description: Invoice AUTO-INV-2026-0006 for ₹76,271,186.44 (+ ₹13,728,813.56 GST) was booked in CA sales and uploaded to GSTR-1, but marked 'UNOFF_SET_UNPAID' on GSTR-3B. Zero customer remittances entered the sovereign bank ledger across 180 days, inflating reported ARR by 57.8%.
red_flags.statutory_citation: Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST) Act 2017 Rule 88C (Tax Discrepancy) & ICAI SA 240 / SA 505 (Auditor Confirmation of Debtors)

red_flags.title: Month-End Cutoff Window Dressing & Contra Capital Infusion
red_flags.description: Temporary capital infusion of ₹28,000,000.00 injected into bank account on Day 28 of reporting month (2026-09-28) to artificially inflate closing cash balance, and drained out 4 days later on Day 2 of the subsequent month.
red_flags.statutory_citation: ICAI SA 240 (Material Misstatement Resulting from Fraud & Cutoff Manipulation) & Companies Act 2013 Section 129

red_flags.title: Section 194C / 194J Mandatory TDS Threshold Smurfing
red_flags.description: 25 repetitive disbursements of exactly ₹49,500.00 executed on the same day (totaling ₹12,37,500.00) to TechCloud Advisory LLP. Structured deliberately ₹500 below the statutory ₹50,000 threshold to evade mandatory 10% TDS deduction under Income Tax Act Section 194C/J.
red_flags.statutory_citation: Income Tax Act 1961 Section 194C, Section 194J & Section 271C (100% Penalty for Willful Tax Deduction Failure)

red_flags.title: Aged Trade Receivables > 180 Days (Uncollected Debtor Stagnation)
red_flags.description: CA General Ledger reflects ₹550,000,000.00 in receivables aged over 180 days with zero recovery in the bank ledger. DSO stands stretched at 146.1 days, indicating uncollectible customer revenue.
red_flags.statutory_citation: Companies Act 2013 Schedule III (Trade Receivables Aging Disclosures) & ICAI SA 505 (External Confirmations)
red_flags.counterparty: Trade Receivables Register (Zenith Retail Tech & Affiliates)

red_flags.title: Income Tax Section 269ST Prohibition of High-Value Cash Receipts (₹2 Lakh Limit)
red_flags.description: Aggregate cash receipt of ₹250,000.00 deposited in a single day (2026-08-14). Violates Income Tax Act Section 269ST (prohibits receiving ₹2,00,000 or more in cash). Attracts 100% penalty of ₹250,000.00 under Section 271DA and signals fictitious revenue channels.
red_flags.statutory_citation: Income Tax Act 1961 Section 269ST & Section 271DA (100% Penalty for Cash Receipts >= ₹2 Lakhs)
